[Bio]: My name is Dmitrii Zhukov. I am a game narrative designer and a published fiction writer. I specialize in mystery-driven worlds, atmospheric horror, and psychologically engaging stories. I create worlds, lore, characters, and interactive narratives that invite players to explore, investigate, and uncover mysteries of the plot through the gameplay.

My first published novel, Myst, became the foundation for Static, a game concept that reimagines the story as a third-person psychological action thriller and survival horror experience.

[Career]: Before moving into narrative design, I worked in the fintech industry as a Senior Technical Writer and Product Documentation Manager. I architected and maintained complete documentation ecosystems (knowledge bases, API documentation, release processes, training materials, and internal collaboration platforms). I also acted as a Product Manager and worked closely with Core, QA, Support, and Customer Success teams. I am proficient in organizing complex information, communicating across disciplines, and turning ideas into structured, user-focused experiences.

[Game writing]: Writing has always been at the core of my career (from technical support instructions to full-time technical writers team lead). It has always been my hobby as well: that is why I have invested a lot of time in writing fiction novels.

After years of creating documentation for complex software products professionally, I chose to bring together my professional experience with my long-standing commitment to fiction writing and game storytelling. Narrative design and worldbuilding allow me to combine structured thinking, collaboration, and clear communication with a passion for creating immersive worlds and meaningful player experiences.

Influences

The stories I invent are shaped by curiosity and observation as much as by fiction as well. Inspiration comes from literature, cinema, video games, music, traveling, education. Visiting XV century castle ruins, listening to a history lecture, or hearing a clever turn of phrase in a song lyric often sparks new ideas: worlds, places, characters, narrative threads. I constantly collect fragments (atmosphere, dialogue pieces, symbolism, plot twists) and then reinterpret them into something new.

• Games: Bloodborne, Control, Alan Wake, The Last of Us, Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice, Death Stranding.

• Films: Drive, It Follows, Se7en, Arrival, Memento, Blade Runner 2049.

• Books: One Hundred Years of Solitude, Blood Meridian, Drood, Harry Potter, Ring, The Langoliers.

• Music: Poets of the Fall, STARSET, The Midnight, The National, Oh Hiroshima, Taylor Swift.

Beyond fiction, I draw inspiration from traveling, exploring historic places, museums, architecture, and learning about the people and events that shaped them. Every place and every individual has a story waiting to be uncovered.
